answer: Simultaneous in-person check-ins limit Sybil accounts in a field survey. At stations surveying sable populations, river ripple patterns, or smoke plume dispersion, marshals verify physical presence and bind each volunteer to one account. Each volunteer stays in a single supervised area for the entire shared check-in window. An attacker needs N people for N accounts, assuming the stations prevent remote check-ins and marshals enforce one check-in per person.
